convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to call external 'Price_Extreme_Indicator' custom indicator which is not a built-in MT5 indicator. The custom indicator must be available and its logic understood or replicated for Python conversion. Standard MQL5 Trade library includes are used but do not add complexity.

derived_values.name: Upper level line from Price Extreme indicator (buffer 0)
Lower level line from Price Extreme indicator (buffer 1)

other_exits: Opposite side positions are closed before entering new direction (CloseSell before Buy, CloseBuy before Sell)

custom_logic_notes: EA requires hedge account (rejects netting accounts). Reverse mode (InpReverce) flips long/short signals. InpSignalsBar (default=1) selects which historical bar to read signals from — uses previous bar by default, not current. Volume is checked against symbol lot limit before entry. StopLevel correction ensures SL/TP respect broker minimum stop distance, using spread*size_spread as fallback when StopsLevel is 0.
python_conversion_notes: The custom indicator 'Price_Extreme_Indicator' must be reverse-engineered or sourced separately — its logic is not available in the EA code. It produces upper/lower price levels from which breakout signals are generated. The EA reads these from buffers 0 (upper) and 1 (lower). The signal bar defaults to bar index 1 (previous completed bar), which is a lookback parameter. SL/TP are in raw points (not pips) and are corrected to respect broker StopLevel. The filling type is auto-detected from symbol properties. Hedge account assumption means simultaneous long/short positions are possible.
